title: Afterhours surge buffer and pin notes (personal)
content:
Purpose:
Quick, messy scratchpad for the late-night small-batch release tomorrow (quiet window). Goal is a minimal-risk flip of model alias -> pinned model-hash with a few extra protection layers for surge and token-cost regressions. Keeping this in my headspace so I can run the checklist with minimal context loss.

High level plan (one-line):
- During off-peak window (01:00–04:00 UTC) perform tenant-safe pin of alias to new model hash, progressively increase traffic across warm cohorts, watch latency/cost/quality signals, and be ready to pin back if any regression.

Assumptions / constraints:
- Target model size: 13B quantized variant (v2026-02-05-hash: 7f3a2c).
- SDK feature-flag exists: rwd-sdk:feature/model-pin (can toggle per-tenant).
- Some high-traffic tenants are scheduled to be excluded from first 30m.
- Burst capacity hedge reserved in Dedicated cluster D-3.

Cohort sequencing (warmup):
1) local-dev clients + internal-prod-test (5% of small set): smoke (0–5m)
2) low-traffic tenants, non-billable flags (0–30m): 10% combined steady ramp
3) neutral tenants (controlled): 30–90m: 30% target fraction across geo/us-eu
4) open ramp to baseline: 90–180m: 100% for cohorts that passed checks

Cohort selection rules:
- Exclude tenants on the holdlist (see linked_artifacts JIRA-INV-4321 for owner list).
- Prefer clients with SDK >= 2.7.0 (supports per-request pin headers).
- Avoid cohorts with concurrent feature launches (check product calendar).

Safety thresholds (immediate rollback if any triggered):
- 5xx rate > 0.8% absolute increase vs baseline (10m sliding)
- p95 latency increase > 200ms and absolute p95 > 800ms (5m sustained)
- Token-per-request cost increase > 12% (30m) or sudden token budget burn spike
- Quality regression: decodingFailures > 0.2% or hallucination alert from content-sentinels

Telemetry & queries to run (quick examples):
- baseline p95: SELECT percentile_cont(0.95) FROM request_latency WHERE model_alias='stable' AND ts > now() - interval '1 hour';
- token cost delta: compute per-request token_delta = (tokens_generated + tokens_prompt) and compare rolling mean 30m
- 5xx spike: SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE status >= 500) / count(*) FROM requests WHERE ts > now()- interval '10 minutes' AND cohort IN (/*cohort ids*/);

Warmup tactics (practical):
- Prefix KV prefill: run a small fanout job that replays common prefixes for top-50 tenants into the KV cache on target nodes (script: scripts/kv-prefill.sh --model 7f3a2c --tenants list.txt). This avoids cold-KV p95 cliffs during first 30m.
- Batch padding: temporarily set sdk.batch_pad=true for cohorts 1–3 to stabilize throughput (only for hosts that tolerate slightly higher cost).
- Soft token cap: enforce per-tenant 10% lower token cap for first 2 hours via quota override to limit blast radius.

Model pin mechanics (notes):
- We will update alias 'stable' -> '7f3a2c' using the control-plane pin API: POST /api/pins {alias: 'stable', model_hash: '7f3a2c', mode: 'gradual', strategy: 'cohort'}
- Use SDK header X-RWD-PIN-TARGET for early cohorts to force pin per-request during testing.
- Ensure console roll-forward flag is set to allow automatic fallback to 'stable@previous' if major errors occur.

Rollback quick commands (CLI snippets):
- Immediate rollback alias: rwdctl model alias set stable --hash=previous-stable-hash --reason='rollback - auto'
- Pin back for a tenant: rwdctl tenant set --id T-345 --pin=previous-stable-hash
- Abort rollout and kill warmup jobs: kubectl delete job kv-prefill-7f3a2c --namespace=release-warmup

Observability watchlist (p0 metrics):
- Global 5xx rate (by cluster and model)
- p95 latency per-region and per-tenant
- Token burn rate (per-tenant) and daily projection
- Error categories: OOM, decodeFailure, timeout, api-bridge-fail
- Sampling of outputs for model-quality (automated eval harness) every 5m for cohorts 2–3

Manual checks at each window boundary (quick checklist):
- [ ] 00:50 UTC: confirm Dedicated reserve ready (ping infra on-call)
- [ ] 00:55 UTC: ensure monitoring dashboards populated and alert suppressions set for noisy infra metrics
- [ ] 01:00 UTC: start cohort 1: enable pin header for internal clients, run smoke tests (sanity prompts list)
- [ ] 01:10 UTC: check p95/5xx/token-cost, KV hit rate; if green, continue
- [ ] 01:30 UTC: move to cohort 2; enable batch_pad and soft caps
- [ ] 02:00 UTC: run sample quality eval (eval-suite/api/v1/sample) and confirm no regression
- [ ] 03:00 UTC: if stable, expand cohorts to 100% as planned; otherwise, hold and decide rollback

Edge cases & gotchas (notes to self):
- Some older SDKs send model alias in body only and ignore header pin; confirm per-tenant SDK version or apply tenant-level pin in control plane.
- KV prefill is not idempotent across node restarts; when a node N is replaced mid-warmup the benefits may be lost — track node-replacement events.
- Billing spikes: remember that token-cost regressions are often correlated with accidental longer completions (prompt mismatch). Keep a short set of anchor prompts that check completion length distribution.

Open questions / followups:
- Who can approve lifting the 10% token cap after 2 hours if the projection still looks conservative? (ping: Evan)
- Confirm Dedicated cluster D-3 burst policy: how many extra GPUs available for 30m peaks? (ask infra)
- Should we pre-seed a small traffic shadow (1%) behind a proxy to get real-request behavior without affecting user metrics? Technical debt: implement shadow proxy in rwd-sdk.

Post-release notes to capture (template):
- Start/stop times, cohorts active, observed metric deltas, any manual interventions, why decisions were made, followup actions, and owners. Save to confluence:Release-Notes/<date>-afterhours-pin.

If I have time before window:
- Run quick dry-run in staging with identical warmup job and capture telemetry for 2h (helps tune thresholds).
- Create a short Slack channel #release-afterhours-<date> and post runbook with pinned checklist.

Misc commands / snippets I keep forgetting:
- Check which tenants are excluded: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://controlplane/internal/tenant-holdlist | jq '.ids'
- Sample eval trigger: curl -X POST https://evaluator/trigger -d '{"suite":"smoke","model":"7f3a2c"}'

Final mental model: small, slow, instrumented. Lean on soft caps and cohort pins, prefer manual expansion rather than aggressive automation for the first afterhours pin. If anything surprises me, pin back quickly and schedule a deeper postmortem rather than risk customer impact.

-- PK
